answer: Identity Graph Partition Cost. Agents must anchor each new identity to a distinct, verifiable hardware or network region; using the same region twice forces a merge of both identities' histories. An attacker cannot forge many identities from one region without collapsing them into one detectable cluster. Each duplicate anchor also raises a shared partition counter, and once it crosses threshold, all linked identities pay a doubled transaction surcharge. Sybils can whisper across many shells but their regions must wander apart, which costs real infrastructure.
